 Follow FEMA approves disaster assistance for 20 Texas counties affected by July flooding, governor's office says
 Marcus Risen Updated Fri, October 30, 2026 at 8:51 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Gov. Greg Abbott has announced that Texas' appeal for Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Individual Assistance program funding has been approved by the federal government. The funding would help those affected by severe storms and flooding in July.
 The approval comes after an announcement from President Trump, noting that his administration would make additional FEMA relief available. It follows an appeal submitted by the State of Texas through the Texas Division of Emergency Management.
 The counties now approved for assistance are Bandera, Bexar, Comal, Crockett, Dimmit, Frio, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Kindle, Kinney, La Salle, Maverick, Medina, Real, Schleicher, Sutton, Uvalde. Val Verde and Zavala. Those affected can apply for FEMA disaster assistance online or by calling 800-621-3362.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The program provides eligible Texans with financial assistance and services for expenses such as temporary housing, emergency homes repairs, uninsured and underinsured personal property losses, disaster legal services, disaster unemployment assistance, and medical, dental and funeral expenses caused by the disaster.
